Subject: Clarify log preservation SLAs and backup exceptions — follow-up

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can put together the docs Novatech needs for procurement/security review.

Recap (high-level)
- SOC 2: you asked if we can provide the latest Type II report and whether we can scope attenuation of audit evidence for a pilot.
- Data protection: GDPR/HIPAA applicability for your healthcare-derived datasets.
- Retention + deletion: you want a clear deletion SLA for user data and a log retention policy that covers active logs and backups.
- Backups: you asked about backup retention windows, RPO/RTO guarantees, and whether backups are immutable or searchable for e-discovery.

Clarifying questions (so we respond precisely):
1) Deletion SLA: is Novatech expecting a per-record deletion confirmation (proof-of-deletion) or is a policy-level SLA (e.g., data removed from primary storage within 30 days + backups within 90 days) acceptable?
2) Logs scope: do you need raw request logs (full headers/token traces), or only redacted/session-level logs for incident investigations?
3) Backups and immutable retention: are there regulatory hold scenarios where backups must be retained beyond the normal retention window?

What we will provide by EOD Monday:
- SOC 2 Type II redacted report (we'll remove customer-identifying exhibits) — see attachment stub.
- A short ops note describing our log retention categories (request logs, access logs, audit logs) and default retention windows.
- Draft language for an SLA and exceptions handling (e.g., legal holds).

Next steps
- If you can indicate answers to the three clarifying questions above, Dylan (cc'd) will prepare the technical appendix.
- If Novatech prefers, we can route the vendor security questionnaire back to you filled with default answers and mark items that require a legal review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with Dylan if you want to walk the appendix together.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks Stephanie — helpful recap. A few answers inline.

1) Deletion SLA: we need per-record deletion confirmation for EU data (GDPR). For US PHI we need deletion within 30 days but certificate-level confirmation is fine.
2) Logs scope: for now we only need redacted/session-level logs for standard ops, but raw request logs will be needed during incident investigations (we will request them ad hoc).
3) Backups and legal holds: yes — we have periodic legal holds. We need a documented process for how Redwood will pause deletion for specific backups and how long those holds can last.

Can you include standard timelines for backup snapshots (daily, weekly, monthly) and the default immutability window? Also confirm whether snapshots are encrypted with a customer-specific KMS key or a Redwood-managed key.

I'll attach Novatech's vendor questionnaire (security@novatech.io) after I confirm internal approval.

— Claire
Claire Hammond

Claire — adding some technical detail to speed things along.

Deletion and backups (short version)
- Primary deletion: we support per-record deletion via API; records removed from primary storage within 24 hours of a deletion request.
- Backups: default snapshot cadence is daily (7-day rolling), weekly (4 weeks), monthly (12 months). Backups are kept in object storage with lifecycle rules.
- Backup immutability: we offer an immutable retention option (WORM) for customers that require it; otherwise backups are lifecycle-managed and removed per policy.
- RPO/RTO: standard Dedicated customers get an RPO of 4 hours for model state and 1 hour for configuration metadata; RTO targets depend on instance sizing and are captured in the Dedicated SLA addendum.

Logs and access
- Logs types: request logs (redacted by default), access logs (full user IDs), audit logs (admin actions).
- Raw request logs are storeable for up to 90 days by default; we can extend on request but will note cost/retention tradeoffs in the ops note.
- For legal holds: we can suspend deletion of specific snapshots or exports; holds are tracked and require an authorized Novatech admin to release.

Encryption/KMS
- Backups are encrypted at rest. For Private deployments we support customer KMS (AWS KMS or customer HSM). For Hosted accounts, we provide an option for customer-managed keys via our KMS integration; otherwise Redwood-managed keys are used.

I can prepare a one-page technical appendix with exact API endpoints, sample deletion request payloads, and the implementation for legal holds. Let me know which depth you need (ops note vs. full API appendix).

— Dylan Brooks
